newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - FEB 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The government is preparing to deregulate the labour market, sources say, without necessarily abolishing the 2.0 percent threshold on mass lay-offs a month. The move is aimed at helping firms facing financial problems or state-run firms facing privatisation.

--The inflow of new capital - both foreign and domestic - on the Athens bourse yesterday brought turnover to over 30 billion drachmas for the second day running and the general price index through the 1,400 point barrier.

--The government will decide final terms for the second attempt to sell Cretabank by next week. The new terms are expected to offer greater flexibility and draw more investors, including the six international and domestic banks which had expressed interest but not bids in the first tender.
--Aspis Pronia announced the expansion of its portfolio yesterday with the purchase of insurance firm Laikis Zois.
--The 1,400 barrier fell yesterday at the Athens bourse in a buying frenzy reminiscent of 1990: brokers say there has been increased real demand by private investors seeking investment alternatives.

--Alpha Credit Bank has returned profits of 60.4 billion drachmas for 1996 and will pay dividends of 925 drachmas per share. The National Housing Bank is expected to announce profits of 41 billion drachmas on Firday.
--Residents abroad will able to file for a return of the tax paid on state titles, according to a new memorandum being drafted by the finance ministry.
--The Bank of Greece has drafted a new memorandum on how to deal with suspicions of money laundering through Greek banks, including a clause lifting confidentiality.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou yesterday announced the government's intentions to attract private investment in the share capital of state-run banks. This participation would not affect either management or ownership of the banks, he clarified. He reiterated plans to merge Commercial and Ionian banks and the National Housing and Mortgage banks.

--The reduction of banks' operating costs will have to begin with a reduction of labour costs, Papandoniou said. The minister said the government would not pressure banks to reduce the difference between lending and deposit interest rates but would be active in pressure for a reduction of their operating costs.

--Lending conditions in the wider public sector have changed with domestic banks able to meet almost all lending needs of public organisations and bodies (DEKOs). Greece's improved credit rating has meant that traditional lenders have had to make their terms far more attractive to stay in the game.

--The government's social dialogue begins tomorrow in the shipping sector with a three-day meeting between Merchant Marine Minister Stavros Soumakis, shipowners and seamen to discuss incentives for the establishment of new shipping firms in Greece and employment issues for seamen.
